questions.stem: A metal block has a mass of 540 g and a volume of 200 cm^3. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = mass / volume = 540 / 200 = 2.7 g/cm^3. This is the density of aluminium. Option A divides volume by mass (the inverse). Option C multiplies instead of dividing. Always use the formula: density = mass / volume.

questions.stem: An object has a density of 0.8 g/cm^3. What happens when it is placed in water (density 1.0 g/cm^3)?

options.text: It remains suspended in the middle of the water

questions.explanation: An object floats if its density is less than the liquid it is placed in. Since 0.8 g/cm^3 is less than water's density of 1.0 g/cm^3, the object floats. This is why oil (density ~0.9 g/cm^3) floats on water and why ice (density ~0.9 g/cm^3) floats. Objects denser than water sink.

questions.stem: A student needs to find the density of an irregularly shaped stone. Which method should they use to find its volume?

options.text: Measure its length, width, and height with a ruler
Place it on a balance and read the volume
Use a displacement method with a measuring cylinder or eureka can
Estimate its volume by comparing it to a known shape

questions.explanation: For irregular shapes, you cannot use length x width x height. Instead, submerge the object in water and measure the volume of water displaced - this equals the volume of the object. A eureka can or measuring cylinder can be used. A balance measures mass, not volume. Estimation is not accurate enough for scientific measurement.

questions.stem: A liquid has a density of 800 kg/m^3. What is the mass of 0.5 m^3 of this liquid?
questions.explanation: Rearranging density = mass / volume gives mass = density x volume = 800 x 0.5 = 400 kg. Option A divides density by volume instead of multiplying. Option C divides volume by density. Option D adds the values, which is physically meaningless.

questions.stem: A solid iron cube (density 7800 kg/m^3) is heated until it melts. Which statement about the density of the liquid iron is correct?

options.text: The density stays exactly the same
The density increases because the particles move faster
The density decreases because the particles are slightly further apart on average
The density doubles because the iron expands

questions.explanation: When a solid melts, the particles gain enough energy to break from their fixed positions and move more freely. They spread out slightly, increasing the volume while the mass stays the same. Since density = mass / volume, a larger volume means lower density. The decrease is small, not dramatic. (Exception: water/ice is unusual because ice is less dense than liquid water.)
